arguments.value: 38-year-old woman with migraine history, chronic anemia, and heavy menses presented with 1 week of severe worsening headache and 3 weeks of right eye vision changes, diplopia, ptosis, and facial paresthesias. Exam showed right ptosis, right-gaze palsy, and ophthalmoplegia consistent with cranial nerve involvement. CT/MRI revealed a 3.2 cm thrombosed right internal carotid artery aneurysm causing cavernous sinus/cranial nerve compression; she was monitored closely, started on aspirin and dexamethasone, and blood pressure was controlled while surgical and endovascular options were considered.
